nodes.summary: Constructs the initial state object for a /history info panel, normalizing screen name, rows, and boolean flags.

nodes.name: setHistoryFlowConversations
nodes.summary: Pushes or replaces the conversations-list entry on the history navigation flow stack, depending on whether the caller came from the dates root or a search jump.

nodes.name: pushHistoryFlowDetail
nodes.summary: Pushes a detail screen (summary or preview) onto the history navigation flow stack above the current conversations screen.

nodes.name: historyBackStep
nodes.summary: Pops one level off the history navigation flow stack (/back command), clearing the whole stack once it empties out of the /history screen entirely.

nodes.name: parseHistoryConversationAlias
nodes.summary: Parses shorthand /history subcommand aliases (e.g. a bare conversation index) out of a raw input line.

nodes.name: normalizeHistoryInputShortcut
nodes.summary: Rewrites a bare shortcut input (a number or alias typed while viewing the conversations screen) into the equivalent full /history command line.

nodes.name: gateway.js
nodes.summary: HTTP client for the chat CLI's calls to the router-gateway: builds auth headers, posts chat-completion requests (streaming or not), decodes routing/model metadata from response headers and payload, and streams assistant text deltas via callbacks.

nodes.name: buildHeaders
nodes.summary: Builds the JSON content-type header and, when an API key is present, an Authorization bearer header for gateway requests.

nodes.name: extractTextContent
nodes.summary: Recursively extracts plain text out of a possibly-array/object-shaped OpenAI-style content field, joining nested text parts.

nodes.name: extractTextFromChoice
nodes.summary: Pulls assistant text out of a single chat-completion choice, preferring the streaming delta content and falling back to the full message content.

nodes.name: extractAssistantTextFromPayload
nodes.summary: Extracts the assistant's text from a full (non-streaming) chat-completion response payload's choices array.

nodes.name: streamChatCompletion
nodes.summary: Posts a chat-completion request to the router gateway, handling both the non-streaming JSON-error-envelope path and the SSE streaming path, decoding routing headers and firing onDelta/onUsage/onRouting callbacks as data arrives.

nodes.name: stream.js
nodes.summary: Minimal Server-Sent-Events parser that reassembles `data:` lines split across network chunk boundaries into complete JSON event objects.

nodes.name: createSSEParser
nodes.summary: Factory returning a stateful SSE parser object (push/flush) that buffers incoming chunks, splits on blank-line event boundaries, and invokes onEvent for each parsed event.

nodes.name: parseEvent
nodes.summary: Parses a single raw SSE event block into its `data:` payload, JSON-decoding it and invoking onEvent, or reporting the terminal `[DONE]` sentinel.

nodes.name: transcripts.js
nodes.summary: Reads and writes chat transcript Markdown files on disk under the vault: builds/parses YAML-ish frontmatter (routing/usage/MMT metadata), derives file-safe local-time filenames and title slugs, and lists transcript dates/files newest-first.

nodes.name: parseFrontmatterValue
nodes.summary: Decodes a single frontmatter scalar value (quoted string with escapes, JSON array, or number) back into its native JS type.

nodes.name: parseFrontmatter
nodes.summary: Splits a transcript Markdown document's leading `---` delimited frontmatter block into a key/value metadata object plus the remaining body text.

nodes.name: summarizeTranscriptTitle
nodes.summary: Derives a filesystem-safe slug title from the first meaningful user message (normalizing accents, stripping URLs/punctuation, capping word count and length), falling back to "chat" when no user message exists.

nodes.name: transcriptFilePath
nodes.summary: Builds the vault-relative transcript file path using the local date folder and an HH-mm-ss--summary-slug filename.

nodes.name: parseTranscriptMarkdown
nodes.summary: Parses a full transcript Markdown document (frontmatter plus role-headed message blocks) into structured metadata and a messages array.

nodes.name: readTranscript
nodes.summary: Reads a transcript file from disk and parses it into structured metadata and messages.

nodes.name: listTranscriptDates
nodes.summary: Lists the vault's transcript date-folder names (YYYY-MM-DD) newest-first.

nodes.name: listTranscriptsForDate
nodes.summary: Lists the transcript files under a given date folder, newest-first by filename, annotated with time and title derived from each filename.

nodes.name: formatTranscript
nodes.summary: Serializes a transcript's metadata and messages into the on-disk Markdown format, embedding routing/usage/MMT frontmatter fields and role-headed message blocks.

nodes.name: writeTranscript
nodes.summary: Computes the transcript's file path from its summary and creation time, formats it, and writes it to disk, creating parent directories as needed.

nodes.name: history.js
nodes.summary: Service layer for the /history feature: builds per-date row summaries, requests an AI-generated transcript summary from the gateway with a timeout/abort guard, and exposes a createHistoryClient factory tying together the date-listing, transcript-summarizing, and per-date-listing collaborators.

nodes.name: createHistoryDateRows
nodes.summary: Builds the /history dates table rows by listing each transcript date folder and counting its entries via the injected listDates/listEntriesForDate collaborators.

nodes.name: createHistorySummaryTimeoutError
nodes.summary: Builds a descriptive timeout error (seconds-rounded) for when a transcript-summary gateway request is aborted.

nodes.name: summarizeHistoryTranscript
nodes.summary: Sends a capped transcript excerpt to the LLM gateway with a summarization prompt, enforcing a timeout via AbortController and returning a short 3-5 sentence summary of the conversation.

nodes.name: createHistoryClient
nodes.summary: Factory assembling the history service's public client object (date rows, per-date transcript listing, summarization) from its injected collaborators.

nodes.name: runtime-config.js
nodes.summary: Loads and validates the MCP server's runtime config (host/port/paths/auth/source-library limits) from config/mcp-server.config.json plus env overrides, enforcing that the server can only bind to a loopback host.
nodes.languageNotes: Calls loadRuntimeEnv() as a top-level module side effect at import time, so env/home-config precedence is baked in before loadMcpRuntimeConfig() ever runs.

nodes.name: normalizeOrigin
nodes.summary: Normalizes an allowed-origin string to its protocol+host form, trimming trailing slashes and falling back to the raw value if URL parsing fails.

nodes.name: isLocalBindHost
nodes.summary: Checks whether a host string is a recognized loopback address (127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1), case- and whitespace-insensitively.

nodes.name: loadMcpRuntimeConfig
nodes.summary: Reads the MCP server config file, applies env-variable overrides (host/port take precedence over the file), throws if the resolved host isn't local, and returns the fully normalized runtime config including auth and source-library limits.

nodes.name: server.js
nodes.summary: Router-gateway process entrypoint: re-exports createGatewayServer for embedding, and when invoked directly, loads runtime config, starts the HTTP server, and logs its bound address plus the upstream LiteLLM base URL.

nodes.name: routing-metadata.js
nodes.summary: Shared codec between the router gateway and the chat CLI: encodes/decodes routing decisions (target model, fallback chain, MMT group) as HTTP response headers on one side and as transcript frontmatter metadata on the other, hiding the internal smart-router alias and surfacing only concrete provider models.
nodes.languageNotes: Central load-bearing contract file referenced by name in CLAUDE.md: the 'smart-router' string is duplicated across router-gateway, chat CLI, and config/router-gateway.json, and this module is where its internal aliasing is decoded away from user-facing output.

nodes.name: isInternalRouteAlias
nodes.summary: Checks whether a value matches one of the routing decision's own internal `_local`/`_cloud` fallback-route aliases, used to avoid re-displaying an internal alias as if it were the resolved model.

nodes.name: serializeRoutingValue
nodes.summary: Serializes a routing metadata value (string, array, or other) into a single header-safe string, comma-joining arrays.

nodes.name: concreteDisplayCandidate
nodes.summary: Picks the first non-smart-router routing field (routed model, target model, fallback entries) to use as the user-facing display model.

nodes.name: decodeRoutingHeaders
nodes.summary: Decodes all routing/model-manager metadata fields (target model, routed model, fallback list, group flags) from an HTTP Headers-like object into a plain routing object.

nodes.name: applyRoutingHeaders
nodes.summary: Writes every populated field of a routing object onto an HTTP response target as serialized headers.

nodes.name: isConcreteRouting
nodes.summary: Determines whether a routing object names a real, non-smart-router model with a concrete provider location.

nodes.name: withResponseModel
nodes.summary: Reconciles the routing object against the model name actually reported in the upstream response payload, promoting a concrete model over the smart-router alias and flagging a local-fallback warning when the executed model contradicts the intended cloud route.

nodes.name: routingFromTranscriptMetadata
nodes.summary: Reconstructs a routing object from a saved transcript's frontmatter metadata fields, the inverse of routingToTranscriptMetadata.

nodes.name: routingToTranscriptMetadata
nodes.summary: Converts a routing object into the flat key/value fields written into a transcript's frontmatter metadata.

nodes.name: notes-automation-gdrive.test.js

nodes.name: notes-automation-glob.test.js

nodes.name: notes-automation-protected-artifacts.test.js

nodes.name: shared-home-config.test.js
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the home-config store covering path resolution, prototype-pollution guards on getPath/setPath, and document projection to and from the env map.

nodes.name: createFakeService
nodes.summary: Test factory building a fake NotesAutomationService with stubbed git and fs collaborators to drive classifyGDriveImport scenarios.

nodes.summary: Test helper that spawns the real git binary synchronously and throws with combined stdout/stderr on non-zero exit.

nodes.name: initRemoteScenario
nodes.summary: Test helper that bootstraps a bare remote git repo and a cloned local checkout for exercising fetch/rebase reconciliation.

nodes.name: createConfig
nodes.summary: Test helper writing a notes-automation config JSON document to disk with sensible git and gdrive sync defaults for the service under test.

nodes.name: withTempCwd
nodes.summary: Test helper that runs a callback with process.cwd() temporarily redirected to an isolated temp directory.

nodes.summary: Test helper creating a paired bare-remote and local git repo scenario used to simulate outbound sync pushes.

nodes.name: withEnv
nodes.summary: Test helper that snapshots process.env, applies overrides, runs a callback, and restores the original environment afterward.

nodes.name: shared-runtime-env.test.js
nodes.summary: Unit tests verifying loadRuntimeEnv's precedence ordering (home config over .env) and its one-time deprecation warning behavior.

nodes.summary: Integration tests for the massa-vault CLI dispatcher (tools/cli.js), exercising install, configure, proxy, and config subcommands via injected fakes and asserting exit codes and usage fallback.

nodes.name: cli.js
nodes.summary: The massa-vault client CLI entrypoint; dispatches install, configure, chat, gdrive, sync, config, and server-proxy subcommands, with every side-effecting collaborator injected behind a named default for testability.

nodes.name: vault-cli-config.js
nodes.summary: Loads the merged runtime configuration for the chat CLI's vault integration, layering built-in defaults, a local JSON config file, and the home-config store.

nodes.name: cli.js
nodes.summary: Thin entrypoint for the notes-automation daemon; re-exports and invokes commands/runtime.js's main(), guarded by the import.meta.url self-execution check.

nodes.name: runtime.js
nodes.summary: CLI command implementations for the notes-automation daemon (start/stop/status/resume/flush-sync/gdrive-check/gdrive-dry-run), orchestrating the daemon service, persisted sync state, and Google Drive checks.

nodes.name: gdrive-import-thresholds.js
nodes.summary: Pure default threshold constants (change and delete percentage limits) used to classify how risky an inbound Google Drive import is.

nodes.name: gdrive-import.js
nodes.summary: Domain logic that classifies inbound Google Drive changes by risk (safe/review/dangerous), computing change statistics and human-readable reasons before a sync commits them.

nodes.name: globs.js
nodes.summary: Pure glob-to-regex conversion and path-matching utility used to evaluate include/ignore watch patterns.

nodes.name: pids.js
nodes.summary: One-line pure helper that normalizes a stored value into a valid positive-integer PID or null.

nodes.name: withEnv
nodes.summary: Test helper isolating process.env mutations per test case and resetting the one-time runtime-env deprecation warning flag between runs.

nodes.name: harness
nodes.summary: Builds a createVaultCli instance wired to recording fakes for runTool/runToolInteractive/log/logError so dispatch behavior can be asserted without spawning real processes.

nodes.name: expectExit
nodes.summary: Test helper asserting that a CLI action throws the ExitSignal sentinel with the expected exit code.

nodes.name: scriptedInterface
nodes.summary: Factory producing a scripted readline-like interface that answers configure()'s interactive prompts from a queued list of canned responses.

nodes.name: parseYN
nodes.summary: Parses a yes/no-ish string answer into a boolean, defaulting when the input is empty or unrecognized.

nodes.name: buildConfig
nodes.summary: Assembles the notes-automation config document from the interactive configure() answers by delegating to createConfigDocument.

nodes.name: createVaultCli
nodes.summary: Factory that builds the massa-vault CLI with every side-effecting collaborator (spawn, fs, readline, git, gdrive, home-config) injected behind named defaults, exposing install/configure/proxy/config subcommand handlers and a dispatching main().
nodes.languageNotes: The `xImpl = x` default-parameter pattern makes every fs/spawn/git/gdrive collaborator swappable in tests without module mocking.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper invoking createVaultCli(options).main(), the production entrypoint used by the module's self-execution guard.

nodes.name: loadVaultCliRuntimeConfig
nodes.summary: Loads and merges the chat CLI's vault runtime config from defaults, a local JSON config file, and the home-config store, resolving relative paths against the config file's directory.

nodes.name: printStatus
nodes.summary: Prints daemon and sync status as JSON, reaping a stale PID file and self-healing the running flag when the recorded process is no longer alive.

nodes.name: startDetached
nodes.summary: Spawns the daemon as a detached background process, writes its PID file, and verifies it survived a short startup grace period.

nodes.name: stopService
nodes.summary: Stops the running daemon by PID (SIGTERM) or cleans up stale state if the process is already gone, exiting non-zero when nothing was running.

nodes.name: requestAction
nodes.summary: Writes a requested action (resume/flush-sync/flush-push) into shared state for the running daemon to pick up, failing if no daemon is active.

nodes.name: summarizeSyncStatus
nodes.summary: Builds a compact sync-status summary object (state, conflicts, gdrive import status) from the persisted daemon state file.

nodes.name: waitForSyncCompletion
nodes.summary: Polls persisted daemon state until the in-flight sync run completes or a timeout elapses, returning the final status summary.

nodes.name: runManualSync
nodes.summary: Triggers a manual sync either by requesting it from a running daemon or executing runSyncOnce directly, then reports the outcome and exit code.

nodes.name: printResolveGuide
nodes.summary: Prints a step-by-step guide for resolving quarantined sync conflicts, or clears the resolved flag and re-triggers sync once the user has finished resolving files manually.

nodes.name: printGDriveCheck
nodes.summary: Loads config and reports whether the configured rclone remote for Google Drive sync is reachable.

nodes.name: printGDriveDryRun
nodes.summary: Runs a dry-run Google Drive sync and prints the result without committing any changes.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Starts the daemon in the foreground, writing its PID and installing SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers for graceful shutdown.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Top-level command dispatcher mapping CLI subcommands (start/stop/status/resume/flush-*/sync-conflicts/sync-resolve/gdrive-check/gdrive-dry-run/run) to their handler functions.

nodes.name: dominant
nodes.summary: Picks the majority key from a frequency map, or null when no entry clears half of the total.

nodes.name: requiresGDriveImportReview
nodes.summary: Returns true when a gdrive import classification is anything other than the safe outcome, signaling the sync should pause for human review.

nodes.name: resolveGDriveImportCommitSubject
nodes.summary: Maps an import classification to the git commit subject line used when the import is auto-committed.

nodes.name: summarizeGDriveImportStatus
nodes.summary: Reduces a persisted sync state's gdrive-import fields into a compact status object for CLI and status-JSON consumers.

nodes.name: classifyGDriveImport
nodes.summary: Core risk-classification engine for inbound Google Drive changes: computes changed/deleted percentages against threshold configs, detects touched protected artifacts, and returns a classification with human-readable reasons and sample paths.

nodes.name: globToRegex
nodes.summary: Compiles a glob pattern (supporting **, *, and ?) into an anchored RegExp for path matching.

nodes.name: matchesGlob
nodes.summary: Tests whether a file path matches any glob pattern in a given list.

nodes.name: asPid
nodes.summary: Coerces a stored value into a valid positive-integer PID, returning null for anything invalid.

nodes.name: protected-artifacts.js
nodes.summary: Domain helpers defining and matching the vault paths (.git, .obsidian, README, .DS_Store, etc.) that notes-automation must never track, commit, or overwrite during sync.

nodes.name: normalizeRelativePath
nodes.summary: Converts a filesystem path to a forward-slash-normalized relative path for cross-platform glob/prefix comparisons.

nodes.name: isProtectedArtifactPath
nodes.summary: Checks a normalized path against the protected artifact glob list to decide whether notes-automation must leave it untouched.

nodes.name: sync-state.js
nodes.summary: Defines the pure factory for the sync sub-state object embedded in daemon state, tracking backend flags, conflicts, and last-run reasons for a single sync cycle.

nodes.name: createSyncState
nodes.summary: Builds a fresh sync-state record with default idle status, empty backend flags, and no conflicts, used to reset or seed daemon state between sync runs.

nodes.name: config-constants.js
nodes.summary: Central default-value constants for notes-automation configuration -- paths, intervals, git/gdrive modes, and the allowed gdrive resync mode set -- consumed by config-definition.js and config.js.

nodes.name: config-definition.js
nodes.summary: Builds the default and merged notes-automation config document (watch paths, include/ignore globs, gdrive args) from the shared config-constants defaults.

nodes.name: createDefaultConfigDocument
nodes.summary: Assembles the full default configuration document object from the individual DEFAULT_* constants, used when no local/home config overrides exist.

nodes.name: createConfigDocument
nodes.summary: Merges a partial config document over the computed defaults to produce the final effective configuration document.

nodes.name: config.js
nodes.summary: Loads and validates the effective notes-automation runtime configuration by layering env vars, home config, and local JSON overrides on top of the defaults, and defines the VaultPathError raised when vault_path is missing.

nodes.name: VaultPathError
nodes.summary: Custom Error subclass thrown when the resolved vault path is missing or invalid, letting callers distinguish configuration errors from other failures.

nodes.name: loadConfig
nodes.summary: Resolves the full runtime configuration by reading the local config JSON, applying home-config and process.env overrides, validating sync-strategy/gdrive-mode enums, and normalizing numeric and glob settings.

nodes.name: daemon-controller.js
nodes.summary: Implements the file-based remote-control channel that lets the CLI request actions (clear-conflicts, force-sync) from the running notes-automation daemon by polling shared state.

nodes.name: createNotesDaemonController
nodes.summary: Builds a controller object whose handleRequestedAction dispatches a pending CLI-requested action (clear-conflicts or force-sync) against the running service and clears the request flag.

nodes.name: pollRequestedAction
nodes.summary: Reads the daemon's persisted state file and, if a control action was requested, hands it to the controller for execution.

nodes.name: daemon-git.js
nodes.summary: Git-facing orchestration layer for the daemon: ensures the vault repo exists, enforces protected-artifact exclusions, commits queued/staged/all changes, and captures pre/post snapshots around Google Drive imports.

nodes.name: ensureVaultGitRepo
nodes.summary: Initializes the vault as a git repo and (re)points its remote if needed, recording the outcome in daemon state.

nodes.name: collectProtectedArtifacts
nodes.summary: Walks the vault tree to find stray .DS_Store files that must be removed before committing, skipping .git internals.

nodes.name: enforceProtectedArtifacts
nodes.summary: Ensures the repo exists, keeps .gitignore entries current, deletes stray .DS_Store files, and untracks any protected paths git may have picked up.

nodes.name: commitStagedWithSubject
nodes.summary: Commits whatever is currently staged under a given subject line, recording the resulting commit hash and a summary of the committed files in daemon state.

nodes.name: commitStagedChanges
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper committing staged changes with a generic manual-sync subject built from a label.

nodes.name: commitQueuedChanges
nodes.summary: Stages only the files queued by the file watcher (skipping protected artifacts) and commits them as a single changeset.

nodes.name: commitAllChanges
nodes.summary: Stages the entire working tree and commits it under a generic label.

nodes.name: commitAllChangesWithSubject
nodes.summary: Stages the entire working tree and commits it under an explicit subject line, used for Google Drive import commits.

nodes.name: isInternalArtifactPath
nodes.summary: Determines whether a path belongs to notes-automation's own internal state directories (.automation, .logs) or a protected artifact, so it can be excluded from Drive-import baselines.

nodes.name: collectInternalArtifactPaths
nodes.summary: Walks the vault tree collecting every internal/protected artifact path so Google Drive import diffing can ignore them.

nodes.name: captureGDriveImportBaseline
nodes.summary: Snapshots the currently git-tracked files plus known internal artifacts, forming the baseline used to classify what a Drive import changed.

nodes.name: createPreGDriveSnapshot
nodes.summary: Stages and commits any pending local changes and records tracked-file state immediately before a Google Drive bisync, giving later steps a clean rollback point.

nodes.name: daemon-watch.js
nodes.summary: Implements the daemon's filesystem-watch layer: native fs.watch per watch-root with an automatic polling fallback and directory-walk snapshotting when native watching fails or is unsupported.

nodes.name: recordWatchFailure
nodes.summary: Appends a capped, timestamped watch-failure entry to daemon state so operators can see why a watch path fell back to polling.

nodes.name: shouldSkipDirectory
nodes.summary: Decides whether a relative path should be skipped while walking the vault, based on .git/.automation suffixes and the configured include/ignore globs.

nodes.name: walkDirectory
nodes.summary: Recursively walks a directory building a snapshot map of tracked file mtimes/sizes, respecting protected-artifact and ignore-glob exclusions.

nodes.name: captureTrackedSnapshot
nodes.summary: Produces a full tracked-file snapshot for a watch root, used both to seed polling and to diff against on each poll tick.

nodes.name: startPollingFallback
nodes.summary: Falls back to interval-based directory polling for a watch root when native fs.watch is unavailable or fails, recording the fallback reason in state.

nodes.name: pollForChanges
nodes.summary: Diffs a fresh directory snapshot against the last tracked snapshot to detect added/changed/removed files and queues them for sync.

nodes.name: watchOne
nodes.summary: Sets up native fs.watch on a single watch root, queuing changed files and switching to the polling fallback on watcher errors or unsupported platforms.

nodes.name: gdrive-constants.js
nodes.summary: Constants for the Google Drive rclone-bisync integration: remote-path example text, resync marker/exit-code conventions, and the exclude/cleanup glob lists layered on top of protected artifacts.

nodes.name: gdrive.js
nodes.summary: rclone-bisync wrapper for syncing the vault with Google Drive: validates remote paths, normalizes bisync args/excludes, detects and recovers from resync-required failures, and runs the actual sync/resync commands.

nodes.name: resolveResyncMode
nodes.summary: Normalizes a configured gdrive resync mode string against the allowed mode set, falling back to the default when unrecognized.

nodes.name: looksLikeLocalPath
nodes.summary: Heuristically detects whether a configured gdrive path is actually a local filesystem path rather than a remote:path rclone reference, to catch misconfiguration early.

nodes.name: listRcloneRemotes
nodes.summary: Lists the rclone remotes configured on the host machine, used to validate and hint about the configured gdrive remote.

nodes.name: validateRcloneRemotePath
nodes.summary: Validates that a configured gdrive remote path is well-formed and references a known rclone remote, producing actionable hints (including available remotes) on failure.

nodes.name: normalizeGdriveArgs
nodes.summary: Normalizes user-configured extra rclone args, merging required excludes with any user-supplied --exclude flags without duplication.

nodes.name: requiresBisyncResyncRecovery
nodes.summary: Inspects a bisync failure's error details to detect the 'missing prior listing' condition that means Drive sync must be recovered via a forced --resync.

nodes.name: resolveSyncCommand
nodes.summary: Maps the configured gdrive sync mode (bisync vs one-way) to the corresponding rclone subcommand.

nodes.name: cleanupGoogleDriveProtectedArtifacts
nodes.summary: Runs an rclone delete pass against the remote to remove any protected-artifact files (like .DS_Store) that leaked onto Google Drive.

nodes.name: prepareGoogleDriveSync
nodes.summary: Builds the full rclone command and argument list for a sync run, validating the remote, resolving the sync command, normalizing args, and flagging first-run resync.

nodes.name: checkGoogleDriveRemote
nodes.summary: Performs a dry, read-only rclone check of the configured remote to verify reachability and configuration before attempting a real sync.

nodes.name: syncToGoogleDrive
nodes.summary: Runs the full Google Drive bisync (or one-way sync), writing a first-run marker, detecting resync-required failures, and automatically retrying with --resync when recovery is safe.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a self-healing retry: on the specific rclone 'no prior listing' failure it re-runs with --resync automatically instead of surfacing a hard error.

nodes.name: git.js
nodes.summary: Thin synchronous wrapper around the git CLI providing the full set of primitives notes-automation needs: add/commit, fetch/rebase/abort, conflict listing and stage reads, ignore-file management, push, and working-tree diffing.

nodes.name: runGit
nodes.summary: Core execFileSync wrapper that runs a git subcommand in a given cwd and returns trimmed stdout, the base every other function in this module builds on.

nodes.name: gitAdd
nodes.summary: Stages a single file path.

nodes.name: gitAddAll
nodes.summary: Stages the entire working tree (git add -A).

nodes.name: gitCachedNames
nodes.summary: Lists the file paths currently staged in the index.

nodes.name: gitCommit
nodes.summary: Commits staged changes with the given message, optionally allowing an empty commit.

nodes.name: gitFetch
nodes.summary: Fetches a remote/branch ref without merging.

nodes.name: gitFetchBranch
nodes.summary: Fetches a specific remote branch, defaulting remote/branch names when omitted.

nodes.name: isRebaseConflictOutput
nodes.summary: Detects git-rebase conflict signatures in captured stderr/stdout text to distinguish real conflicts from other rebase failures.

nodes.name: gitRebaseOnto
nodes.summary: Rebases the current branch onto an upstream ref, classifying failures as conflicts vs other errors.

nodes.name: gitAbortReconcile
nodes.summary: Aborts an in-progress rebase (falling back to merge --abort) to return the repo to a clean state after a failed reconcile.

nodes.name: gitListConflictedFiles
nodes.summary: Lists paths currently in an unmerged/conflicted state in the index.

nodes.name: gitReadStageFile
nodes.summary: Reads a specific conflict stage (1/2/3) of a file's content, used to extract 'ours'/'theirs' versions during conflict quarantine.

nodes.name: gitListTracked
nodes.summary: Lists tracked files matching optional pathspecs, used to find protected artifacts that git already tracks.

nodes.name: sync-run.js
nodes.summary: The full sync pipeline for notes-automation: quarantines git conflicts, pulls/rebases inbound git changes, runs the Google Drive bisync and classifies its import, pushes outbound git changes, and coalesces concurrent sync requests into a single queued run.
nodes.languageNotes: quarantineGitConflicts writes git conflict stage 2 to an 'ours' path and stage 3 to 'theirs' -- correct for a merge, but pullGitInbound reconciles via git rebase, where the stages are inverted (stage 2 is actually the remote tip, stage 3 the local commit). This is a live, verified mislabeling: a user trusting 'ours = my edit' during manual conflict resolution can silently overwrite their own work with the remote's.

nodes.name: createNotesAutomationAdapters

nodes.name: quarantineGitConflicts
nodes.summary: Moves every conflicted file's base/ours/theirs versions plus a manifest into a timestamped quarantine folder and clears them from the working tree, so a rebase can complete non-interactively.

nodes.name: pullGitInbound
nodes.summary: Fetches the remote branch and rebases local commits onto it, quarantining conflicts and aborting the rebase automatically if reconciliation fails.

nodes.name: syncGoogleDriveInbound
nodes.summary: Runs the Google Drive bisync step and records its outcome (success, conflict quarantine info, or failure reason) into daemon sync state.

nodes.name: pushGitOutbound
nodes.summary: Pushes committed local changes to the git remote, recording push failures (like non-fast-forward) distinctly in sync state.

nodes.name: handleSuccessfulGDriveImport

nodes.name: executeSyncRun
nodes.summary: Runs one full end-to-end sync cycle -- enforce artifacts, commit queued changes, pull, snapshot, sync Google Drive, classify the import, and push -- updating sync state at every step and short-circuiting on the first failure.

nodes.name: runQueuedSync

nodes.name: unquote
nodes.summary: Strips matching single/double quotes from a raw .env value and unescapes common backslash sequences (\n, \r, \t, \", \\) inside double-quoted values.

nodes.name: stripInlineComment

nodes.name: parseEnvContent

nodes.name: loadLocalEnv
nodes.summary: Locates and parses a .env file relative to the given base directory and merges its values into process.env, never overwriting an already-set key unless override: true is passed.

nodes.name: home-config.js
nodes.summary: The user-owned home config store shared across all tools: resolves ~/.config/massa-ai-vault/config.json (honoring XDG_CONFIG_HOME and the off-switch env var), maps its dotted document paths to the 23-entry env-key vocabulary, and tolerates malformed JSON by degrading gracefully.
nodes.languageNotes: readHomeConfig() never throws on a malformed file -- it degrades to { loaded: false } so a broken home config can't crash every tool that starts up.

nodes.name: getPath
nodes.summary: Reads a dotted-path value (e.g. sync.push_interval_min) out of a nested config document object.

nodes.name: setPath
nodes.summary: Writes a value into a nested config document at a dotted path, creating intermediate objects (via Object.create(null)) as needed.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Object.create(null) plus Object.hasOwn guards for the intermediate objects specifically to prevent prototype-pollution via attacker-controlled dotted paths.

nodes.name: resolveHomeConfigPath
nodes.summary: Resolves the home config file's absolute path, honoring MASSA_VAULT_HOME_CONFIG (including an off value to disable it entirely) and XDG_CONFIG_HOME.

nodes.name: projectHomeConfigEnv
nodes.summary: Pure projection of a home-config document into the flat env-var shape, using HOME_CONFIG_ENV_MAP to translate dotted paths to env key names.

nodes.name: readHomeConfig
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the home config JSON file from disk, returning { loaded: false } if disabled, missing, or malformed rather than throwing.

nodes.name: applyHomeConfigEnv
nodes.summary: Loads the home config and applies its projected env values onto process.env, first-writer-wins like the .env loader.

nodes.name: readHomeConfigSection

nodes.name: buildHomeConfigDocument

nodes.name: runtime-env.js

nodes.name: loadRuntimeEnv

nodes.name: createUsageCommandSpecs

nodes.name: shared.js

nodes.name: createHistorySelectionUsage

nodes.name: info-screen.js

nodes.summary: Builds an escaped markdown table string from header and row arrays, guarding against non-array inputs.

nodes.name: mcp-server-answer-sessions.test.js

nodes.name: withMockEmbeddings

nodes.name: search.js

nodes.name: embedTexts
nodes.summary: Calls the configured embeddings HTTP endpoint with a batch of texts and returns their vector embeddings, validating the response shape.

nodes.name: isIndexStale
nodes.summary: Compares the file snapshot stored in a cached search index against the current vault snapshot to decide whether the index needs rebuilding.

nodes.name: buildSearchIndex
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the vault's semantic search index from scratch: lists Markdown files, chunks their contents, embeds each chunk in batches, and persists the resulting index with a snapshot for staleness checks.

nodes.name: ensureSearchIndex
nodes.summary: Loads the persisted search index and rebuilds it only if the vault scope changed or the index is stale relative to the current files.

nodes.name: searchIndex
nodes.summary: Ranks indexed chunks by cosine similarity against a freshly embedded query, optionally scoped to an allow-list of file paths, and returns snippet-annotated top results.

nodes.name: getSearchDefaults
nodes.summary: Returns the default search tuning parameters (result limit, minimum score, ignore globs) used when callers don't override them.

nodes.name: normalizeFilterPaths
nodes.summary: Normalizes a list of caller-supplied file paths (slashes, leading './') into a canonical form used to scope search results.

nodes.name: listMarkdownFiles
nodes.summary: Walks the vault directory tree iteratively, applying include/ignore glob filters, and returns the relative paths of all Markdown files to index.

nodes.name: splitIntoChunks
nodes.summary: Splits a document's text into overlapping fixed-size chunks suitable for embedding, so long notes are searchable at paragraph granularity.

nodes.summary: Computes the cosine similarity between two embedding vectors, guarding against mismatched lengths and non-numeric components.

nodes.name: extractSnippet

nodes.name: state.js

nodes.name: http.js

nodes.name: writeJson
nodes.summary: Writes a JSON response with the given status code and sets the appropriate content-type header.

nodes.name: jsonRpcError

nodes.name: readJsonBody

nodes.name: extractBearerToken

nodes.name: textResult
nodes.summary: Wraps a payload into the MCP tool-result content shape, JSON-stringifying it as a single text content block.

nodes.name: errorResult
nodes.summary: Converts a thrown error into an MCP-compatible error tool result, preserving a machine-readable code and message.

nodes.summary: Wires together the MCP server's dependency graph — vault config loading, source library, retrieval, answer sessions, grounded-answer, and auth — into a single services object consumed by the tool handlers.

nodes.summary: Registers every MCP resource and tool (list/read sources, add/update/remove sources, search, ask, select-sources, cleanup) against the MCP SDK server instance, validating inputs with zod and routing to the wired services.

nodes.name: server.js

nodes.name: handleAuthRoute
nodes.summary: Dispatches the auth sub-routes (login, refresh, logout) for the MCP HTTP server, translating auth-service results and errors into JSON responses.

nodes.name: requireAuth
nodes.summary: Extracts and validates the bearer token on incoming MCP requests, returning the authenticated session or writing a 401 JSON error.

nodes.name: handleMcpRequest
nodes.summary: Handles a single MCP JSON-RPC HTTP request end-to-end: checks the request origin, requires auth, spins up a fresh MCP server/transport pair, and tears it down after the response.
nodes.languageNotes: Creates a brand-new MCP server and transport per request rather than reusing a long-lived connection, closing both once the response completes.

nodes.name: createMcpHttpServer
nodes.summary: Builds the Node http.Server instance that routes requests to the auth routes or the MCP endpoint based on URL path, loading runtime config and services up front.

nodes.name: startMcpServer

nodes.name: answer-sessions.js

nodes.name: createAnswerSessionStore

nodes.name: auth.js

nodes.name: AuthError
nodes.summary: Custom error type for authentication failures, carrying a machine-readable error code alongside the message.

nodes.name: createAuthService
nodes.summary: Factory for the session-based auth service: issues access/refresh token pairs, verifies credentials with timing-safe comparison, and implements login, refresh, logout, and authenticate against in-memory session/token maps.

nodes.name: grounded-answer.js

nodes.name: formatRetrievedContext

nodes.name: buildClarification
nodes.summary: Builds a clarification response (and suggested follow-up questions) when a question is empty, no sources are selected, or no relevant context was retrieved.

nodes.name: createGroundedAnswerService
nodes.summary: Factory for the grounded-answer service: resolves the active source scope, retrieves and formats supporting context, calls the chat gateway with conversation history, and records/returns the answer along with its sources.

nodes.name: source-library.js

nodes.name: SourceLibraryError
nodes.summary: Custom error type for source-library validation failures, carrying a machine-readable error code.

nodes.name: normalizeSourceId
nodes.summary: Validates and trims a caller-supplied source id against the allowed id pattern, rejecting malformed ids.

nodes.name: normalizeVaultRelativeMarkdownPath
nodes.summary: Normalizes a user-supplied path into a vault-relative, forward-slashed Markdown file path, rejecting absolute paths, parent-directory escapes, and non-.md files.

nodes.name: sourceUriForId
nodes.summary: Builds the canonical MCP resource URI for a source id, used both when registering resources and when resolving them back to an id.

nodes.name: sourceIdFromUri
nodes.summary: Extracts and normalizes the source id from an MCP resource URI or request variables, decoding percent-encoding.

nodes.name: resolveSourcePathInVault
nodes.summary: Resolves a vault-relative path to an absolute file path and verifies, via realpath comparison, that it stays inside the vault root and points at a real file — the core defense against path-traversal and symlink escapes.

nodes.name: normalizeTags
nodes.summary: Deduplicates, trims, and sorts a list of source tags into a canonical form for storage and comparison.

nodes.name: readLibraryFile
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the source-library JSON file from disk, defaulting to an empty library if the file is missing or malformed.

nodes.name: makeSourceEntry
nodes.summary: Builds a new source-library entry record (id, path, title, description, tags, timestamps, enabled flag) from a create/update payload.

nodes.name: createSourceLibrary
nodes.summary: Factory for the persisted source library: loads/saves the JSON-backed catalog and implements list/get/getMany/add/update/remove with path validation, duplicate-path/id checks, and tag filtering.

nodes.name: source-retrieval.js

nodes.name: createSourceRetrievalService
nodes.summary: Factory bridging the source library and the vault search index: lists and reads sources as MCP resources, and runs semantic searches over the vault scoped to a caller-selected set of sources.

nodes.name: server-processes.test.js

nodes.summary: Parses server CLI arguments (run/start/stop/restart/status, --json, --only) and dispatches to a constructed ServerSupervisor, printing human-readable or JSON status output.

nodes.name: process-state.js
nodes.summary: Pure domain functions for constructing and interpreting server/service state shapes: empty state creation, pid normalization, per-service state derivation from config, and running-state summarization.

nodes.summary: OS-level process helpers wrapping process.kill: isProcessRunning probes liveness via signal 0, sendSignal delivers a termination signal, both tolerating invalid pids and platform-specific errno codes (EPERM/ESRCH).

nodes.name: state.js

nodes.summary: Writes a temporary server.config.json fixture with state/pid paths under a temp dir and a default or overridden services map.

nodes.summary: Returns a fake spawn() implementation producing an EventEmitter child with stdout/stderr PassThrough streams and a synthetic kill() that emits an exit event, recording spawn/kill calls for assertions.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses CLI argv into a command (defaulting to status), a --json flag, and one or more --only service selectors, throwing on unknown options.

nodes.name: printStatus
nodes.summary: Prints supervisor status either as pretty-printed JSON or a human-readable running/stopped summary with per-service pid/ownership annotations.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry function that parses argv, constructs a ServerSupervisor via createRuntime, and dispatches to run/start/stop/restart/status, exiting with an error for unrecognized commands.

nodes.name: createEmptyServerState
nodes.summary: Builds the default/empty server state shape (versioned, no pid, not running, empty services map) used as a fallback when no state file exists.

nodes.name: normalizePid
nodes.summary: Coerces a value to a positive integer pid or null, used throughout the supervisor to defend against malformed persisted state.

nodes.name: serviceStateFromConfig
nodes.summary: Derives a fresh per-service state record (status, health url, timestamps, error fields) from a service's static config entry.

nodes.name: isOwnedServiceRunning
nodes.summary: Determines whether a service is running and owned (not external) by checking its recorded pid against a supplied process-liveness probe.

nodes.name: summarizeServerRunning
nodes.summary: Determines whether the supervisor process itself is currently running by checking its recorded pid against a supplied process-liveness probe.

nodes.name: isProcessRunning
nodes.summary: Checks whether a pid is alive by sending signal 0 via process.kill, treating EPERM (permission denied but process exists) as running and any other error as not running.

nodes.name: sendSignal
nodes.summary: Sends a termination signal (default SIGTERM) to a pid via process.kill, returning false if the process no longer exists (ESRCH) and rethrowing other errors.

nodes.name: ServerStateStore

nodes.name: ServerSupervisor

nodes.name: CI
nodes.summary: Primary GitHub Actions workflow, gating every push and pull request against master through a single Node-25-matrixed `test` job: checkout, install, lint (oxlint correctness rules), a tracked-secret scan, an `install.sh --check-only` bootstrap check, a CHANGELOG-presence gate for pull requests, and the full test suite. Its workflow name `CI` is load-bearing because release.yml triggers on a `workflow_run` of exactly that name, and its job id (reported as `test (25)`) is one of the two required status-check contexts on the master ruleset.
nodes.languageNotes: The workflow's `name: CI` is a string contract consumed by release.yml's `workflow_run: workflows: [CI]` trigger — renaming it silently breaks the release chain with no diff in release.yml itself. Separately, the required-status-check context is the job id `test (25)` (matrix-suffixed), not the workflow name.

nodes.name: Coverage
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow whose single `coverage` job checks out the repo, installs dependencies, and runs `node --test --experimental-test-coverage` against ratchet-floor thresholds (lines 88 / branches 72 / functions 86) on every push and pull request to master, with no `continue-on-error` so a failing floor genuinely blocks the run. Kept as a workflow deliberately separate from CI so a coverage regression can block a merge without ever being able to misfire the release chain that hangs off the `CI` workflow name.
nodes.languageNotes: The required-status-check context that a branch ruleset references is the job id `coverage`, not the workflow's display name `Coverage` — the two are easy to conflate but govern different things.

nodes.name: Release
nodes.summary: Automatic release workflow whose single `release` job is gated on a completed, successful `CI` run on master (or manual dispatch): derives the next semver from the CHANGELOG's `[Unreleased]` section via `scripts/release-version.js`, commits the version bump with a `[skip ci]`-marked message, tags and pushes atomically using the release-bot deploy key to bypass branch-protection restrictions that block a plain `GITHUB_TOKEN` push, and publishes the GitHub Release from the derived notes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `workflow_run` rather than `push`/`push: tags` specifically because a `GITHUB_TOKEN`-authored tag/release raises no further workflow event (GitHub's recursion guard); the deploy-key push does raise events, which is exactly why the bump commit's `[skip ci]` marker is load-bearing to avoid an infinite retrigger loop.

nodes.name: .env.example

nodes.name: .oxlintrc.json

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Primary contributor guide describing the five-process architecture (router-gateway, notes-automation, mcp-server, llm-chat-cli, server supervisor), the domain/infrastructure/services/commands/cli layering convention, the tools/shared cross-package contract layer, load-bearing string constants, and the CI/release mechanics including the required 'CI' workflow name and the release deploy-key bypass.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: User-facing overview of the Massa Vault System: architecture summary, git/Google-Drive sync backend behavior, massa-vault CLI usage (install/configure/chat/sync/status/config), the router-gateway, Model Manager Tools, and security notes.

nodes.name: install.sh
nodes.summary: Interactive/noninteractive bootstrap script that checks system prerequisites (Node >=25, npm, git, python3, curl), installs LiteLLM into a local Python venv, writes .env and config/notes-automation.local.json, migrates settings into the home config, configures the external vault's git remote, installs security hooks, pulls Ollama models, validates the setup, and optionally starts services.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `set -euo pipefail` plus a layered resolve_config (CLI flags > env vars > existing local config > interactive prompt) before any file is written, and shells out to small inline `node -e` scripts (json_value, set_env_value, write_local_config) for JSON reading/writing that bash can't do natively.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Root package manifest for the massa-vault-tools monorepo: declares the two CLI bin entrypoints (massa-vault, massa-vault-server), pins Node >=25.9.0, and defines the npm scripts wrapping setup, service supervision, chat/sync client actions, linting, security scanning, and release versioning.

nodes.name: usage
nodes.summary: Prints the install.sh CLI usage banner listing all supported flags (--yes, --check-only, --start/--no-start, --vault-path, sync/git/gdrive options, --skip-model-pull).

nodes.name: confirm
nodes.summary: Prompts the user for a yes/no confirmation, auto-confirming without prompting when running in --yes noninteractive mode.

nodes.name: install_package
nodes.summary: Installs a missing system package via Homebrew on macOS or apt-get/dnf on Linux, offering to install Homebrew first if absent, and dies with an error in --check-only mode or if no supported package manager is found.

nodes.name: ensure_command
nodes.summary: Verifies a required CLI command is on PATH, delegating to install_package to install it via the platform package manager when missing.

nodes.name: ensure_node_version
nodes.summary: Ensures the installed Node.js major version is >=25, attempting to install/upgrade Node via the platform package manager if the running version is too old, and warning instead of failing in --check-only mode.

nodes.name: ensure_litellm_python
nodes.summary: Searches for a Python 3.10-3.13 interpreter compatible with the pinned LiteLLM version among common binary names, installing Python 3.13 as a fallback when none is found.

nodes.name: json_value
nodes.summary: Reads a single top-level key's value out of a JSON config file via an inline Node.js one-liner, printing nothing if the file or key is absent.

nodes.name: prompt_value
nodes.summary: Prompts the user for a value with an optional default shown in brackets, returning the default when the user presses enter without typing anything.

nodes.name: normalize_choice
nodes.summary: Lower-cases and validates a value against a space-separated allow-list (e.g. sync strategy git/gdrive/both), dying with a descriptive error when the value isn't one of the allowed choices.

nodes.name: normalize_bool
nodes.summary: Normalizes assorted truthy/falsy string inputs (true/yes/y/1, false/no/n/0) into the literal 'true' or 'false', dying on anything else.

nodes.name: validate_rclone_remote_path_syntax
nodes.summary: Validates that a Google Drive remote path follows rclone's remote:path syntax, rejecting values that look like local filesystem paths (leading /, ./, ../, ~/, or a Windows drive letter).

nodes.name: verify_rclone_remote_exists
nodes.summary: Confirms the rclone remote named in a remote:path value is actually configured locally, listing the available remotes in the error message when it isn't found.

nodes.name: set_env_value
nodes.summary: Upserts a single KEY=value line into the .env file via an inline Node.js script, replacing an existing key in place or appending a new line if the key isn't present.

nodes.name: migrate_home_config
nodes.summary: Runs `node tools/cli.js config migrate` to build the user-owned home config from .env and config/notes-automation.local.json when no home config exists yet; skipped entirely in --check-only mode.

nodes.name: ensure_env_file
nodes.summary: Creates .env from .env.example on first run, generates a fresh LITELLM_MASTER_KEY when the placeholder value or --force is set, and in --check-only mode reports .env and home-config presence instead of writing anything.

nodes.name: resolve_config

nodes.name: security-scan-secrets.test.js

nodes.name: install-hooks.sh
nodes.summary: One-shot setup script that points git's core.hooksPath at .githooks and makes the pre-commit/pre-push hooks executable.

nodes.name: scan-secrets.js
nodes.summary: Standalone secret scanner used by the git hooks: lists staged or all tracked files, filters to likely-text content, and matches each against known secret patterns (API keys, private keys, refresh tokens, bearer tokens), exiting non-zero and blocking commit/push on any match.
nodes.languageNotes: Detection is purely regex-pattern heuristics over file content sampled for text-likelihood — a pragmatic, low-dependency approach rather than a full entropy-based secret scanner.

nodes.name: utcToday
nodes.summary: Returns today's date in UTC as YYYY-MM-DD, matching the changelog's dated release heading format.

nodes.name: unreleasedBounds
nodes.summary: Locates the line indices bounding the `## [Unreleased]` changelog section, throwing if the heading is missing rather than guessing a version.

nodes.name: extractUnreleased
nodes.summary: Extracts the raw text of the Unreleased changelog section using the bounds computed by unreleasedBounds.

nodes.name: unreleasedHeadings
nodes.summary: Parses the Unreleased section body into a deduped set of lowercased ### heading names that contain at least one non-blank content line, so an empty heading cannot force a release bump.

nodes.name: decideBump
nodes.summary: Maps changelog heading names to a semver bump class: minor-class headings win over patch-class, and no qualifying heading yields no release.

nodes.name: nextVersion
nodes.summary: Computes the next X.Y.Z version from a current semver string and a minor/patch bump, never incrementing the major component; throws on a non-semver input.

nodes.name: unreleasedNotes
nodes.summary: Produces the trimmed Unreleased section body to use as the GitHub release notes.

nodes.name: promoteChangelog
nodes.summary: Rewrites CHANGELOG.md by inserting a fresh empty Unreleased section and promoting the previous Unreleased body under a new dated version heading, leaving every other section untouched.

nodes.name: deriveRelease
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the release derivation: reads package.json and CHANGELOG.md, decides the bump class, computes the next version, and — unless dry-run — writes both files back to disk.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README explains what this repository actually is: a tooling-only automation system for a personal Obsidian vault, with no notes of its own. It lays out the five cooperating pieces — an AI routing gateway, a git/Google-Drive sync daemon, an MCP grounded-source server, an Ink chat TUI, and a supervisor that manages them — and the client CLI that ties them together. Keep this map in mind; every later step drops into one of these five boxes.

tour.title: The Client Entry Point
tour.description: `tools/cli.js` is the `massa-vault` binary and the project's actual entry point: it dispatches to install, configure, chat, gdrive, sync, config, and server-proxy subcommands. Every side-effecting collaborator it needs — filesystem, network, process spawn — is injected behind a named default parameter rather than mocked at the module level, a pattern you'll see repeated in every tool in this repo. This single file is the jumping-off point for the chat flow (Step 9) and the sync flow (Step 6) covered later.
tour.languageLesson: Dependency injection via named defaults (e.g. `{ fetchImpl = fetch }`) is this codebase's alternative to a DI framework or module-level mocking — it keeps production code and test doubles symmetric with zero extra tooling.

tour.title: How the Codebase Is Organized
tour.description: CLAUDE.md is the contributor guide, and it defines the layering convention every tool follows: domain/ (pure transforms, no I/O) → infrastructure/ (all fs/network/spawn) → services/ (orchestration) → commands/ (wiring) → cli/ (entrypoints guarded by an `import.meta.url` check). It also documents that these five tools are not independent packages — there is one root package.json, and cross-tool imports are normal and expected. Understanding this layering now means every file you see in Steps 5-9 will already make sense by its directory alone.

tour.title: Shared Contracts: Config and Env Precedence
tour.description: Before looking at any individual tool, meet the layer they all depend on. `tools/shared/env.js` is the repo's only `.env` parser, `home-config.js` resolves the user-owned `~/.config/massa-ai-vault/config.json` store, and `runtime-env.js` composes both into the documented precedence: process.env > home config > `.env`, each a first-writer-wins assignment. Every tool bootstrapped from Step 2 onward reads its configuration through this exact chain, so a change here ripples across the whole system at once.
tour.languageLesson: First-writer-wins assignment (never overwrite an already-set key unless told to) is how this repo achieves layered config precedence without a config-merging library — later loaders simply skip keys the earlier loader already claimed.

tour.title: The Router Gateway
tour.description: The router-gateway is the AI traffic cop: `gateway.js` validates an incoming chat request, `classifier.js` scores it into a code/multimodal/general lane by phrase matching, and `model-resolution.js` picks a concrete model by complexity tier before proxying to LiteLLM. `server.js` is the process entrypoint that wires this together and starts listening. The lane keywords and confidence floor themselves live in `config/router-gateway.json`, keeping routing policy out of code and editable without a redeploy.
tour.languageLesson: Notice `classifier.js` and `model-resolution.js` live under domain/ as pure functions — where they must read a file, that fs read is isolated in a thin `loadX(path)` wrapper so the scoring logic itself stays a pure function testable with in-memory fixtures.

tour.title: Notes Automation and Sync
tour.description: `daemon-service.js` is the composition root for the sync side of the system: it wires config plus git/gdrive/watch infrastructure into a single daemon object. `sync-run.js` is the actual pipeline invoked on every run — quarantine conflicts, pull/rebase inbound git changes, run the Google Drive bisync, push outbound changes, all serialized so a second sync request while one is in flight gets coalesced rather than run concurrently. `config/notes-automation.config.json` supplies the vault path, watch globs, and git/gdrive tuning that this pipeline reads on startup.

tour.title: The MCP Grounded-Source Server
tour.description: `mcp.js` assembles the MCP server's service graph — source library, retrieval, answer sessions, grounded answer, auth — and registers the tools/resources that let an AI client search and cite vault Markdown as grounded sources. `server.js` is the HTTP entrypoint wiring auth routes and the JSON-RPC endpoint behind an origin check and bearer-token guard. `answer-sessions.js` is worth calling out on its own: it is the one piece of state in this entire repo that is deliberately in-memory only rather than persisted to JSON, because a chat session's turn history doesn't need to survive a restart.

tour.title: The Service Supervisor
tour.description: `ServerSupervisor` is what actually starts the router-gateway (Step 5), the MCP server (Step 7), and the notes-automation daemon (Step 6) together, plus LiteLLM. It health-probes each service's `health_url` before spawning — if a service is already running externally, the supervisor marks it `external: true` and never touches it — and it rolls back everything it started if any single service fails to come up. `config/server.config.json` declares the four managed services with their spawn commands and health-check URLs, and `tools/server/src/cli.js` is the thin entrypoint that runs this supervisor as the `massa-vault-server` binary invoked by Step 2's `start`/`stop`/`status` commands.

tour.title: The Chat CLI and Ink TUI
tour.description: This is the other half of what `tools/cli.js` dispatches to. `cli/main.js` is the composition-root entrypoint that parses arguments and decides whether to launch the full interactive Ink TUI (`ink-repl.js`) or a plain-text REPL depending on TTY support. Unusually for this codebase, the command layer here is inverted: `commands/runtime.js` assembles slash-command families that receive every side-effecting operation through an injected `deps` bag rather than importing services directly, and `command-executor.js` is the composition root that builds that bag. `config/vault-cli.config.json` supplies the gateway URL and smart-router defaults this whole flow talks to.
tour.languageLesson: Ink renders React components to the terminal instead of the DOM — `InkChatApp` in ink-repl.js uses ordinary React state/hooks for message history, input handling, and status display, just targeting a different renderer.

tour.title: The Glue Between Tools
tour.description: Two tiny shared modules let independently-running processes agree on a data shape without a shared server. `routing-metadata.js` is the codec the router-gateway (Step 5) uses to encode its routing decision into HTTP response headers, which the chat CLI (Step 9) then decodes and persists into transcripts. `sync-status-contract.js` and `sync-status-model.js` play the same role between notes-automation (Step 6, the producer) and the chat CLI (the consumer) for sync-status display — a frozen enum vocabulary plus a pure function that normalizes the daemon's raw state JSON into something a UI can render directly.

tour.title: Bootstrap and Security
tour.description: `install.sh` is how a fresh checkout becomes a running system: it checks prerequisites (Node, npm, git, python3), installs LiteLLM into a local Python venv, and writes the initial `.env`/config files that Step 4's env-precedence chain will later read. `scan-secrets.js` is the standalone scanner that the pre-commit and pre-push hooks run — installed by `install-hooks.sh` pointing git's `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks` — to block commits containing likely secret patterns before they ever reach history.
tour.languageLesson: Shell scripts here follow the same fail-fast discipline as the JS code: prerequisite checks run before any mutating step, so a missing dependency stops the bootstrap instead of leaving a half-configured system.

tour.title: CI, Coverage, and Release
tour.description: Three GitHub Actions workflows gate everything that lands on master. `ci.yml`'s job id `test (25)` is a required status check, and its workflow name `CI` is itself load-bearing — `release.yml` triggers on a `workflow_run` of exactly that name, so renaming either breaks the release chain silently. `coverage.yml` is deliberately kept separate so a coverage-floor regression can block a merge without being able to misfire a release. `release.yml` derives the next version from the CHANGELOG's `[Unreleased]` section and pushes the tagged bump using a deploy key that can bypass branch protection, since a plain `GITHUB_TOKEN` push cannot.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions' `workflow_run` trigger lets one workflow react to another workflow's completion by name — powerful for chaining release automation onto CI, but it means the triggering workflow's name becomes an unenforced string contract other files depend on.

tour.title: How Everything Gets Tested
tour.description: The test suite is flat `tests/*.test.js` files using plain `node:test` with no `describe`/`it` nesting, importing straight into the `tools/` layers you've now toured. `neutralize-home-config.js` is the one non-test helper in that directory — it has the highest fan-in of any file in this repository because it must be the first import of any test that transitively reaches Step 4's `runtime-env.js`, forcing `MASSA_VAULT_HOME_CONFIG=off` before that module's static import evaluates. Without it, a developer's real home config could leak into a test run and break the promise that this suite is machine-independent — exactly the kind of cross-tool contract this whole tour has been showing you.
